question: How much will Nasdaq-100 Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 10-trading-day windows of Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 price return. 2026 YTD (+15.8% vs +11.9% through Sep 16) implies ~+0.21pp per biweekly window, in line with the 2010-2025 drift, so the prior median is small and positive. Adjustments are close to offsetting: yields at the highest since 2007 (10y ~4.96-5.0%), a Fed hiking to 3.75-4.00% today with dot-plot risk, and oil >$105 on Hormuz/Houthi disruption all favor SPX's energy/financial/industrial weights over long-duration tech, while NDX carries the memory-pricing supercycle, far higher EPS growth (45.6% vs 28.8% in Q1), and a Micron report on Sep 30 inside the window. Late September is also the weakest seasonal stretch, and NDX's ~1.15 beta means a down tape costs it the spread, so I keep the median near zero (+0.10) with a left-skewed body. Dispersion is the dominant feature: 2026 has produced +5.2, +5.3 and -6.6pp monthly spreads, so a 10-day 10-90 width of ~4.2pp is justified even with VIX only ~16-17. Evidence quality was mixed - retrieved pages gave mutually inconsistent index levels - so I weighted the monthly return series over point quotes and stayed near the base rate.
